item.title: France: French Competition Authority fines Apple €150M for implementation of App Tracking Transparency systems

item.title: Spain: AEPD fines GEO ALTERNATIVA €20,000 for unlawful data processing
item.description: On December 20, 2024, the Spanish data protection authority (AEPD) published its decision in Proceeding No. PS/00492/2023, in which it imposed a fine of €20,000 on GEO ALTERNATIVA, S.L. (GEOAL) for a violation of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), following a complaint.Background to the decisionThe complainant stated that GEOAL had included the complainant's data in the ASNEF register of defaulters over a debt that the complainant had already reached an agreement on. item.title: Germany: DSK calls for amendments to BDSG and employee data protection law
item.description: On March 27, 2025, the German Data Protection Conference (DSK) issued a press release on its 109th conference held on March 26 and 27, 2025. In particular, the DSK stated that it adopted key points for a digital future based on freedom and fundamental rights.What are the key proposals?The DSK requested for the following, among others, during the conference.Finalize amendments to the Federal Data Protection Act (implementing the GDPR) (BDSG) and the employee data protection law. The DSK proposed, among other things, a central regulation of responsibilities for nationwide issues and the institutionalization of the DSK with an office. item.title: EU: Commission publishes Digital Europe Program work program for 2025-2027
item.description: On March 28, 2025, the European Commission announced that it published its work program 2025-2027 of the Digital Europe Program, targetting the implementation of, among other things, the EU Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act), the EU Digital Identity Wallet, the Cyber Solidarity Act, and the Cyber Resilience Act, as well as the Interoperable Europe Act. What is included in the work program?The work program outlines as one of its objectives to integrate and adopt the Apply AI Strategy in the EU by focusing on the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in Europe, contributing to the deployment of generative AI applications, AI usage in the health and care sector, virtual worlds

item.title: Germany: BaFin publishes instructions for information register under DORA
item.description: On March 31, 2025, the Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin) announced the publication of instructions for submitting the information register under the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA). What are the key instructions from BaFin?The BaFin stated, among other things, that the information register is intended to provide an overview of all contracts with information and communication technology (ICT) service providers, i.e., ICT third-party service providers, who provide ICT services to the financial company. item.title: UK: ICO issues guidance on anonymization
item.description: On March 28, 2025, the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) released its guidance on anonymization. What does the guidance cover?The guidance outlines key concepts of anonymization and pseudonymization within the UK legal framework, explores identifiability and risk management approaches, and discusses how pseudonymization supports data protection compliance. item.title: Romania: ANSPDCP fines NTT Data Romania RON 124,430 following a data breach

item.title: Utah: Governor signs bills on AI and privacy
item.description: On March 25, 26, and 27, 2025, the Governor of Utah signed a series of bills relating to artificial intelligence (AI) and privacy.Regarding AI bills, the Governor signed the following legislation:Senate Bill 271 on Unauthorized AI Impersonation, which clarifies the circumstances where an individual's identity is abused when used by AI;Senate Bill 226 on AI Transparency, which requires the disclosure of the use of AI in high-risk consumer interactions;House Bill 452 on AI and Mental Health, which outlines requirements relating to the use of AI and generative AI in the context of mental health cases and advertisement, and disclosures for when AI is used; andSenate Bill 180 for Law Enforcement

item.title: Vietnam: Prime Minister promulgates list of important and core data
item.description: On March 25, 2025, the Prime Minister of Vietnam promulgated a list of important and core data. item.title: China: CAC requests comments on draft amendments of cybersecurity law

item.title: Taiwan: Executive Yuan passes draft act organizing Personal Data Protection Commission
item.description: On March 27, 2025, the Executive Yuan announced that it approved the draft Personal Information Protection Commission Organization Act (the draft act) and the draft amendments to the Personal Data Protection Act 2010 (as amended in 2015) (PDPA) (the draft amendments) prepared by the Preparatory Office of the Personal Information Protection Commission.Key provisions of the draft actThe Executive Yuan outlined that the key provisions of the draft act include:the purpose of establishing the Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC);the procedures relating to the functioning and establishment of the PIPC; the organizational structure of the PIPC; andthe tasks and responsibilities of the

item.title: China: CAC launches special actions on personal information protection in 2025
item.description: On March 28, 2025, the Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) announced that it will work with the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, the Ministry of Public Security, the State Administration for Market Regulation, and other departments to carry out several special actions in 2025 to address the illegal and irregular collection and use of personal information in common service products and common life scenarios.What is the scope of the special actions?The CAC outlined that the special actions will address the illegal collection and use of personal information in, among other things:apps; software development kits (SDK);smart terminals, such as wearable products, home products

item.description: On March 27, 2025, the Data Security Council of India (DSCI) published Privacy Pulse 2024-2025. item.title: New York: AG recommends consumers delete data from 23andMe accounts
item.description: On March 25, 2025, the New York Attorney General issued recommendations for consumers regarding their genetic data following 23andMe's bankruptcy filing. The AG provided instructions for consumers to delete their data and destroy any DNA samples held by 23andMe.You can read the press release here.

item.description: On March 27, 2025, Senate Bill 71 for an act relating to consumer data privacy and online surveillance passed its third reading in the Senate. item.title: EU: Commission publishes draft Regulation on subcontracting RTS under DORA
item.description: On March 24, 2025, the European Commission published a draft Regulation containing the Regulatory Technical Standards (RTS) for subcontracting under the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), following an opinion issued by the European Supervisory Authorities (ESAs).What are the provisions of the draft RTS?The draft RTS provides standards for subcontracting ICT services supporting critical or important functions, as required in Article 30(5) of DORA. item.title: UK: IAB UK responds to ICO draft guidance on storage and access technologies
item.description: On March 25, 2025, the Interactive Advertising Bureau (IAB) UK published its response to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) draft guidance on storage and access technologies.What are IAB UK's concerns?Among other things, the response discusses  IAB UK's concerns about the potential impact of the guidance on the digital advertising ecosystem and the wider online economy. item.title: Kenya: Ministry of Information, Communications, and Digital Economy publishes National AI Strategy
item.description: On March 27, 2025, the Ministry of Information, Communications, and Digital Economy published the final Kenya National Artificial Intelligence (AI) Strategy 2025 –2030. This follows public consultation on the strategy, which began in January 2025.What is contained in the strategy?The strategy is based on three key pillars, specifically:artificial intelligence (AI) digital infrastructure - which entails the development of accessible and affordable AI infrastructure and a modernized national digital infrastructure for AI access and development;data - which seeks the establishment of a sustainable data ecosystem for AI and innovation; andAI research and innovation - developing localized AI mode
